name: How do you match a new extension to an existing Spanish or traditional LA home?

mainEntity.name: How do you match a new extension to an existing Spanish or traditional LA home?
mainEntity.text: How do you match a new extension to an existing Spanish or traditional LA home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Matching a new extension to an existing Spanish or traditional Los Angeles home starts with scale and roof form. If the massing feels wrong, even high-quality finishes will not make the addition look authentic. The design should echo the original roof pitch, stucco texture, window proportions, and exterior material palette without becoming a fake replica. In many cases, the best approach is a modern but compatible extension that respects the original architecture. Interior transitions matter too, because floor levels, ceiling heights, and opening sizes should flow naturally from old to new. Homeowners should ask for elevation drawings and 3D views before construction so they can judge how the addition will read from the street and backyard. A well-designed extension should improve the home visually as well as functionally, especially in neighborhoods where architectural character affects resale appeal.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use compatible rooflines, proportions, materials, window shapes, and trim details so the addition looks original to the house. The goal is not to copy every detail exactly, but to make the new work feel intentional and architecturally consistent.
